newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's AvtoVAZ to issue shares for debt.
newsitem.headline: Russia's AvtoVAZ to issue shares for debt.

text.p: Russia's biggest carmaker AvtoVAZ will restructure its tax debt by issuing a controlling stake of new shares in the company to the government, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Friday.

"A decision has been taken to restructure AvtoVAZ's debt in accordance with government order 254," Chubais told reporters at a briefing, referring to a government plan unveiled earlier this year to allow companies to restructure their debt.

"Tomorrow that question will be put to the shareholders meeting and in a month's time an extraordinary shareholders meeting will be called where the decision to issue the shares will be taken," said Chubais, who is also finance minister .
Under the restructuring plan, the companies must issue new equity comprising a controlling stake to be held as collateral by the state or company debt that can also be held by the state.
If the companies fail to pay their debt, the government can sell the shares or bonds. The government has threatened to sue companies which do not pay or restructure with bankruptcy.
Chubais said he had agreed the debt restructuring plan with AvtoVAZ chief executive Vladimir Kadannikov in Moscow in what he described as a difficult conversation.
The agreement covered a schedule of debt payments by AvtoVAZ to federal and regional governments, he said.

"If schedule is broken, then AvtoVAZ loses the controlling stake and the management structure of the enterprise will be changed," Chubais said. He did not say what the deadline for restructuring AvtoVAZ's debt was.
The Russian economy is struggling with massive non-payments and parliament is due to consider controversial government proposals in June to cut planned 1997 expenditure by one fifth.
AvtoVAZ is one of Russia's biggest corporate debtors, with a debt to the government of 2.81 trillion roubles ($487.2 million) as of May 1.
